questions.q: Describe the major types of farming practised in India.
answer: Farming in India varies with physical environment, technology and social customs.

answer.text: Practised on small patches with primitive tools and family labour, it depends on the monsoon and natural soil fertility. It is a slash-and-burn form of farming, called jhumming in north-east India, where land is cleared, cultivated and then left to recover.
Found in densely populated regions, it is labour-intensive, using high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation on small holdings to raise output.

Here modern inputs such as high-yielding seeds and fertilisers are used to produce for the market. Plantation farming is a type of commercial farming in which a single crop like tea, coffee or rubber is grown on large estates.

answer: Thus Indian agriculture ranges from primitive to highly commercial forms.

questions.q: Distinguish between the rabi, kharif and zaid cropping seasons.
answer: Indian agriculture follows three main cropping seasons, shaped by the monsoon and the annual weather cycle.

answer.text: Rabi crops are sown in winter, from October to December, and harvested in summer, from April to June. Important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard, grown mainly in the north and north-west.
Kharif crops are grown with the onset of the monsoon and harvested in September and October. They include rice, maize, jowar, bajra, tur, cotton, jute and groundnut.
Zaid is a short season between rabi and kharif, in the summer months, producing watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops.

answer: These seasons allow different crops to be grown through the year.
